On the other hand, some studies have shown that exercise can be beneficial for osteoarthritis management, particularly when combined with other treatment modalities [1]. For example, a study found that modest weight loss plus moderate exercise provided the greatest improvement in knee pain and mobility [1]. Furthermore, regular exercise can improve mood, increase flexibility, and promote heart health [1]. It is essential to note that the type and intensity of exercise are crucial, and high-impact aerobic activities may accelerate the breakdown of cartilage in weight-bearing joints [1]. Low- or no-impact aerobic activities, such as swimming, walking, and bicycling, are excellent ways to improve fitness without putting excessive stress on the joints [1]. It is recommended to work with a physical therapist to develop an exercise program tailored to individual needs and abilities [1]. The program should include a balance of range-of-motion, muscle-strengthening, and aerobic exercises [1].
